title: Remote Sensing Platforms and Sensors
text: abstract: Remote sensing is the acquisition of information about an object without coming in physical contact of that object. And ‘sensor’ is a device that helps in gathering of information (amount of EMR emitted or reflected by the object). In other words, ‘sensor’ is the remote sensing device that records wavelengths of energy. Generally, these sensors are mounted or fixed with a ‘platform’. Therefore, ‘platform’ is termed as a vehicle that carries remote sensing device. | type: Remote Sensing Sensor Types

title: A Study of Types of Sensors used in Remote Sensing | International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunication
text: abstract: Of late, the science of Remote Sensing has been gaining a lot of interest and attention due to its wide variety of applications. Remotely sensed data can be used in various fields such as medicine, agriculture, engineering, weather forecasting, military tactics, disaster management etc. only to name a few. This article presents a study of the two categories of sensors namely optical and microwave which are used for remotely sensing the occurrence of disasters such as earthquakes, floods, landslides, avalanches, tropical cyclones and suspicious movements. The remotely sensed data acquired either through satellites or through ground based- synthetic aperture radar systems could be

title: A Study of Types of Sensors used in Remote Sensing | International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunication
text: used to avert or mitigate a disaster or to perform a post-disaster analysis. | type: Remote Sensing Sensor Types

title: Remote Sensing Data Preprocessing Technology
text: abstract: With the development of remote sensing technology, remote sensing images are becoming increasingly convenient. Different types of remote sensing images have different advantages in urban green space research. This chapter mainly introduces the characteristics and preprocessing methods of multi-spectral high-resolution data, LiDAR point cloud data, Quickbird image data, etc. Apart from these, the latest street view map, a type of real time map service, provides 360° panoramic views of cities, streets or others. The service provides users the maps with an immersive browsing experience. Street view data has gradually become the data source of urban green space research due to its

title: Remote Sensing Data Preprocessing Technology
text: similarity to pedestrian perspective and low acquisition cost. | type: Data Acquisition and Preprocessing

title: Satellite image formation and preprocessing methods
text: abstract: This paper gives a conceptual and practical introduction to the field of satellite image formation and preprocessing. In particular, the process of satellite image generation is discussed going through each step of its lifecycle. A special explanatory emphasis is given to the process of remote sensing and further mapping and fusion of satellite imagery within acquired segments of electromagnetic spectrum. Moreover, methods of satellite imagery retrieval have been practically demonstrated. The satellite imagery data has been extracted from Sentinel 2 dataset and analyzed with Python language image processing libraries. | type: Data Acquisition and Preprocessing

title: Data Acquisition And Preprocessing Techniques For Remote Sensing Field Research
text: abstract: A crops and soils data base has been developed at Purdue University's Laboratory for Applications of Remote Sensing using spectral and agronomic measurements made by several government and university researchers. The data are being used to (1) quantitatively determine the relationships of spectral and agronomic characteristics of crops and soils, (2) define future sensor systems, and (3) develop advanced data analysis techniques. Researchers follow defined data acquisition and preprocessing techniques to provide fully annotated and calibrated sets of spectral, agronomic, and meteorological data. | type: Data Acquisition and Preprocessing

title: Integrated Methodology for Atmospheric Correction and Cloud Removal of Multispectral Remote Sensing Images Using Guided Diffusion Model
text: abstract: The atmospheric correction and cloud removal are core tasks of the atmospheric radiative transfer model in satellite remote sensing radiometric calibration. The accurate atmospheric correction and cloud removal of satellite remote sensing images are critical preliminary steps for effective satellite remote sensing applications. Current methods for atmospheric correction and cloud removal in satellite remote sensing imagery are mainly divided into traditional algorithms and deep learning methods. | type: Data Acquisition and Preprocessing

title: Improved Vicarious Radiometric Calibration Method Considering Adjacency Effect for High Resolution Optical Sensors
text: abstract: When using field calibration site to perform on-orbit radiometric calibration for a space-borne remote sensor, the observed signal of the sensor may contain energy from adjacent pixels, due to existence of the earth atmosphere and sensor viewing characteristics. Hence the accuracy of radiometric calibration will be decreased to some extent. When calibration of high-resolution sensor is concerned, the non-uniformity of the ground target will be relatively more obvious. | type: Data Acquisition and Preprocessing

title: Atmospheric correction algorithms for hyperspectral remote sensing data of land and ocean
text: abstract: Hyperspectral imaging data have been collected with different types of imaging spectrometers from aircraft and satellite platforms since the mid-1980s. Because the solar radiation on the sun-surface-sensor path in the 0.4–2.5 µm visible and near-IR spectral regions is subject to absorption and scattering by atmospheric gases and aerosols, the hyperspectral imaging data contains atmospheric effects. In order to use hyperspectral imaging data for quantitative remote sensing of land surfaces and ocean color, the atmospheric effects must be removed. | type: Data Acquisition and Preprocessing

title: Supervised Vicarious Calibration (SVC) of hyperspectral remote-sensing data
text: abstract: A full-chain process approach to extracting reflectance information from hyperspectral (HRS) data which is valid for all sensor qualities is proposed. This method is based on a mission-by-mission approach, followed by a unique vicarious calibration stage. As the HRS sensor's performance may vary in time and space, a vicarious calibration method to retrieve accurate at-sensor radiance values is necessary. | type: Data Acquisition and Preprocessing

text: abstract: Fine spatial resolution remote sensing images are crucial sources of data for monitoring the Earth's surface. Due to defects in sensors and the complicated imaging environment, however, fine spatial resolution images always suffer from various degrees of information loss. According to the basic attributes of remote sensing images, the information loss generally falls into three dimensions, that is, the spatial, temporal and spectral dimensions. | type: Spatial, Temporal, and Spectral Resolutions

The data from a single satellite sensor is sometimes insufficient to fulfil the expanding needs of remote sensing applications. Spatial-temporal fusion techniques have become an effective way for merging spectral data from many sources and times, enabling improved data analysis and interpretation. | type: Spatial, Temporal, and Spectral Resolutions

Accuracy of temporal variation is an important guarantee for achieving fidelity fusion in STSF. | type: Spatial, Temporal, and Spectral Resolutions

However, owing to budget and sensor technology constraints, a single sensor cannot simultaneously provide observational images with both high spatial and temporal resolution. This brings difficulties to remote sensing research which requires high spatial and temporal resolution data. | type: Spatial, Temporal, and Spectral Resolutions

title: Synthetic Aperture Radar
text: intro: The azimuth resolution of conventional real aperture radar depends on the dimension of the antenna and on the distance from the target. To achieve very high resolution in azimuth | content: The azimuth resolution of conventional real aperture radar depends on the dimension of the antenna and on the distance from the target. To achieve very high resolution in azimuth, a very narrow beam is required. To get a very narrow beam, extremely long physical antenna is necessary. It is very difficult to build an antenna of several kilometers in length and operate from space. Therefore, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) was developed to overcome the limitation of keeping long antenna in space. SAR

title: Synthetic Aperture Radar
text: systems use an antenna of much smaller physical dimensions, which sends pulses from different positions as the platform advances, simulating a synthetic aperture by integrating the pulse echoes into a composite signal. Aperture means the opening used to collect the reflected energy that is used to form an image. In the case of a camera, this would be the shutter opening, for radar it is the antenna. SAR can provide better resolution than conventional real aperture radars. By proper post processing important information can be extracted from the high resolution images acquired by SAR. The advantage of using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is that the spatial resolution is independent of

title: Synthetic Aperture Radar
text: platform altitude. Therefore, fine resolution can be achieved. Generally images are acquired in strips as the sensor moves along its flight path. These strips are called as swaths (the area illuminated by the antenna which is elongated and elliptical in shape). To separate the objects in the range direction (perpendicular to flight path), radar echoes are separated using the time delay between echoes that are backscattered from the different scatterers. To separate the objects in azimuth direction (parallel to the flight path) Doppler frequency is used. Since time delay and Doppler frequency is used to separate the objects on the Earth surface, the resolution is independent of the distance

title: Synthetic Aperture Radar
text: between the radar and the target.

title: Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR)
text: intro: Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) revolutionized radar remote sensing by providing detailed insights into the characteristics of objects and terrain through their scattering properties. | content: In comparison with traditional systems that were based on single-polarization information, the main feature of PolSAR is its capability to both transmit and receive microwave signals in multiple polarizations, such as vertical (V), horizontal (H), and cross-polarizations (HV or VH). This technology allows PolSAR to gain the total polarimetric scattering information, namely the amplitude and the phase of the received signal, to conduct a detailed analysis of the scattering

title: Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR)
text: process. As a result, PolSAR improves the differentiation capability between various target types, such as vegetation, man-made structures, and natural features, making it a versatile tool for applications in agriculture, forestry, and land cover classification. With the launch of dedicated PolSAR satellites, the technology has become more accessible and widespread, enabling global monitoring and comprehensive Earth observation. Ongoing research continues to refine PolSAR processing techniques, enhancing its capabilities in fields like terrain analysis, environmental assessment, and target recognition. As it evolves, PolSAR remains at the forefront of radar remote sensing, providing a

title: Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR)
text: valuable perspective on our planet's dynamic features and complex environments.

title: Polarization Correlation
text: intro: Polarization correlation in polarimetry explains the degree of correlation or relation between the polarization states of the radar waves. | content: Within the context of Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR), polarization correlation is a fundamental concept explaining the relations among different combinations of polarization states. It is divided into two main forms: co-polarization and cross-polarization. Co-polarization refers to the relationship between horizontal (H) and vertical (V) polarization states of the radar waves. In PolSAR, HH (horizontal transmit and horizontal receive) and VV (vertical transmit and vertical receive) are co-polarized signals. High

title: Polarization Correlation
text: co-polarization indicates that radar waves maintain a strong correlation in their polarization states. Cross-polarization refers to the correlation between horizontal transmission and vertical reception (HV) or between vertical transmission and horizontal reception (VH). These channels represent cross-polarized signals. Low cross-polarization suggests that the polarization states are weakly correlated, which is often indicative of surface or volume scattering.

title: Interferometry
text: intro: Interferometry is a remote sensing technique using radar imagery to measure surface deformation or topography through the interpretation of phase differences between two or more radar images of the same scene. | content: The phase of a radar signal contains information about the distance between the radar sensor and the target surface. An interferogram results from comparing the phase values generated from two radar signals: the interferogram exhibits a change in distance from the sensor to the ground for each of its corresponding images. This phase difference responds very sensitively to any kind of slight displacement resulting from earthquakes, landslides, or subsidence as well as

title: Interferometry
text: to variations in elevation. Factors that contribute to the quality of phase information include wavelength, baseline distance (the separation between the sensor positions), and the surface roughness. Interferometry is highly sensitive, capable of measuring minute changes on Earth's surface on the order of millimeters, making it a powerful tool for studying Earth's dynamics.

title: Ball Corporation
text: Ball Corporation, through its subsidiary Ball Aerospace, plays a significant role in the remote sensing domain by developing advanced technologies for Earth observation. Notable contributions include the successful completion of environmental testing for the WorldView-3 satellite, which features innovative sensors designed to enhance image quality and atmospheric monitoring capabilities. Ball Aerospace also demonstrated its methane remote sensing technology during the Mobile Monitoring Challenge, effectively detecting methane leaks with high spatial resolution. Additionally, Ball's Operational Land Imager 2 (OLI-2) instrument was launched aboard NASA's Landsat 9 satellite, further solidifying its commitment to providing precise and reliable remote sensing solutions. The company has a rich history of pioneering advancements in aerospace systems and continues to support various applications in environmental monitoring, national security, and scientific research. For more detailed information about their remote sensing.

title: BlackSky
text: BlackSky is a geospatial intelligence company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. It operates a constellation of 60 small satellites in low Earth orbit, providing high-frequency satellite imagery and analytics through its proprietary Spectra AI software platform. BlackSky serves various sectors, including government and commercial enterprises, with applications ranging from national security to environmental monitoring. The company is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol BKSY and has established itself as a leader in the geospatial market, known for its agile tasking system that allows rapid data collection and analysis. With a growing business pipeline and significant contracts with government agencies, BlackSky is well-positioned to meet the increasing demand for real-time Earth observation services.

title: BM Geoinformatics
text: BM Geoinformatics is an emerging geospatial company based in India, specializing in a range of services including Building Information Modeling (BIM), GIS mapping, 3D laser scanning, and photogrammetry. Established in 2011 and located in Kolkata, the company aims to revolutionize construction and urban planning by integrating advanced technologies into its workflows.

title: Capella Space
text: Capella Space is an innovative American company specializing in Earth observation through Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology. Founded in 2016 by Payam Banazadeh and William Walter Woods, the company is headquartered in San Francisco, California, with additional offices in Washington, D.C., and Louisville, Colorado. Capella Space aims to revolutionize how industries access and utilize geospatial data. By providing timely and reliable SAR imagery, the company supports critical decision-making processes across various sectors, contributing to a deeper understanding of global changes and challenges.

title: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC)
text: The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) is a major state-owned enterprise responsible for the development and manufacturing of spacecraft, launch vehicles, and ground equipment in China. Established in 1999, CASC has its roots in the country's aerospace initiatives dating back to 1956. It plays a central role in China's space program and is involved in various sectors, including military and civilian aerospace applications. CASC oversees multiple subsidiaries and research academies, focusing on missile systems, satellite technology, and space exploration. The corporation has made significant contributions to national projects such as manned space missions and lunar exploration. In addition to its core aerospace functions, CASC is involved in producing machinery, chemicals, and communications equipment, reflecting its diverse industrial capabilities. The corporation's strategic focus includes innovation-driven development and enhancing China's position in global aerospace markets.

title: Descartes Labs
text: Descartes Labs is a technology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Santa Fe, New Mexico. It specializes in automating the analysis of geospatial data to provide actionable insights for various sectors, including agriculture, resource exploration, and climate resilience. The company leverages satellite imagery and advanced analytics to help organizations address critical global challenges, such as food security and environmental monitoring.

title: Dhruva Space
text: Dhruva Space is an Indian aerospace manufacturer headquartered in Hyderabad, founded in 2012 by Sanjay Srikanth Nekkanti. The company specializes in developing small satellites for commercial, governmental, and academic markets, providing full-stack space-engineering solutions that encompass the design, launch, and operation of satellites. Dhruva Space has gained recognition for its innovative capabilities, including the successful testing of its Satellite Orbital Deployer and the launch of amateur radio communication CubeSats as part of ISRO's missions. Dhruva Space has received several awards for its contributions to the space sector and continues to pursue ambitious projects, including collaborations with various organizations and upcoming missions to validate its nanosatellite platforms.

title: ESRI
text: Esri, founded in 1969 by Jack and Laura Dangermond, is a leading global provider of geographic information system (GIS) software, renowned for its flagship product, ArcGIS. Headquartered in Redlands, California, Esri has established itself as a pioneer in spatial analytics and location intelligence, serving over 350,000 organizations worldwide, including government agencies, businesses, and educational institutions. The company focuses on leveraging geospatial technology to address complex societal challenges such as climate change and urban planning. With a commitment to innovation and sustainability, Esri invests significantly in research and development to enhance its offerings. The company's diverse workforce of over 6,000 employees collaborates with a vast network of partners to deliver effective GIS solutions that empower users to make informed decisions based on geographic data.

title: Fototerra Atividades de Aerolevantamentos Ltda
text: Fototerra Atividades de Aerolevantamentos Ltda, founded in 1993, is a Brazilian company based in Macaé, Rio de Janeiro, specializing in aerial surveying and geospatial data generation. The company provides high-resolution imagery, Lidar data, hyperspectral imaging, and radar data services. Fototerra positions itself as a leader in the information technology sector, focusing on innovative solutions and new business opportunities within the architecture, engineering, and design industries. With a workforce of 100 to 249 employees, Fototerra is recognized for its expertise in leveraging advanced technologies to deliver comprehensive geospatial intelligence and support various projects across different sectors.

title: Genesys International Corporation Limited
text: Genesys International Corporation Limited, established in 1995 and headquartered in Mumbai, India, is a leading provider of advanced mapping, survey, and geospatial services. The company specializes in Geographic Information Systems (GIS), LiDAR, aerial imagery, and 3D mapping technologies. With a workforce of over 2,000 professionals, Genesys has successfully executed numerous projects across various sectors, including urban development, telecommunications, and infrastructure.

title: Gomspace APS
text: GomSpace ApS is a Danish company specializing in the design, manufacture, and operation of nanosatellites for various applications, including defense, academic research, and commercial markets. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Aalborg, Denmark, GomSpace has developed a reputation for its innovative nanosatellite platforms and constellation operations management. The company has successfully launched several missions, such as the GomX-4 satellites, which demonstrated advanced capabilities like inter-satellite communication and high-resolution imaging. GomSpace is also expanding into the microsatellite domain, with recent contracts aimed at developing new platforms for enhanced signal intelligence and surveillance. With a focus on integrated solutions and cutting-edge technology, GomSpace is positioned as a leader in the small satellite industry.

title: Google Earth Engine
text: Google Earth Engine (GEE) is a cloud-based platform for planetary-scale geospatial analysis, combining a vast catalog of satellite imagery and geospatial datasets with powerful computational capabilities. It enables users, including researchers and developers, to perform complex analyses on large amounts of data for applications such as environmental monitoring and mapping. GEE provides access to extensive datasets from satellites like Landsat and Sentinel, offering both interactive and batch processing modes through JavaScript and Python APIs. The platform also includes machine learning tools for efficient model development. While free for academic and research use, commercial applications require a subscription. GEE is essential for tracking environmental changes and assessing climate impacts.

title: Gray Routes Technology Pvt. Ltd
text: Gray Routes Technology Pvt. Ltd. is a prominent provider of location analytics and field automation software, headquartered in Mumbai, India. Founded in 2015, the company specializes in offering geospatial data and tools that facilitate territory and inventory planning, as well as sales force automation (SFA) implementation.

title: HERE Technologies
text: Here Technologies is a Dutch multinational company specializing in mapping technologies and location data services. Established in 1985 as Navteq, it was acquired by Nokia in 2007 and rebranded as HERE in 2012. The company is majority-owned by a consortium of German automotive manufacturers, including Audi, BMW, and Mercedes-Benz, along with Intel holding a stake.

title: ICEYE
text: ICEYE is a Finnish company that designs, builds, and operates a constellation of synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) satellites. ICEYE's satellites provide near real-time imaging of Earth, which can be used for monitoring and responding to changes.

title: ImageSat International
text: ImageSat International (ISI) is an Israel-based company specializing in satellite photography and data decoding services, primarily for security agencies. Founded in 1999, ISI has established itself as a leader in space-based intelligence solutions, providing high-quality satellite observation services and analytics powered by artificial intelligence. The company operates a constellation of advanced satellites, including the EROS series, which offer ultra-high-resolution imagery for various applications. ISI's capabilities encompass the development of mission-effective satellite systems and multi-satellite command and control ground systems, enabling persistent surveillance and strategic intelligence gathering. With a workforce of approximately 105 employees, ISI continues to innovate in the field of geospatial intelligence, serving some of the world's most demanding defense and intelligence organizations.

title: Indian Space Research Organization
text: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is India's national space agency, established on August 15, 1969, with the objective of harnessing space technology for national development. Headquartered in Bengaluru, ISRO operates under the Department of Space (DOS) and has played a pivotal role in advancing India's capabilities in satellite communication, remote sensing, and space exploration. The organization is known for developing reliable launch vehicles like the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) and the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV), which have made significant contributions to both national and international satellite launches. ISRO's projects include a wide array of applications such as weather forecasting, disaster management, telemedicine, and education through its extensive fleet of satellites. The agency also emphasizes scientific research and education, conducting missions like the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) and the Chandrayaan lunar missions. With a commitment to future readiness, ISRO is actively pursuing advancements in heavy-lift launchers, reusable vehicles, and human spaceflight initiatives

title: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA)
text: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) is the national space agency of Japan, established on October 1, 2003, through the merger of three organizations: the National Space Development Agency (NASDA), the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science (ISAS), and the National Aerospace Laboratory of Japan (NAL). Headquartered in Tsukuba, Ibaraki, JAXA is responsible for a wide range of activities including satellite development, space exploration, and aeronautics research. JAXA's mission encompasses promoting satellite utilization to enhance quality of life, advancing scientific knowledge about the universe, exploring celestial bodies like the Moon and Mars, and ensuring the operation of the International Space Station (ISS). The agency also focuses on developing rocket technologies to meet diverse launch needs and conducting fundamental engineering research for autonomous space activities. With approximately 1,500 staff members, JAXA operates several research centers and facilities across Japan, including the Tanegashima Space Center for rocket launches and the Earth Observation Research Center in Tokyo. The agency is known for its motto "One JAXA" and its corporate slogan "Explore to Realize," reflecting its commitment to utilizing space for societal benefits. JAXA continues to play a pivotal role in international space collaborations and advancements in aerospace technology

title: KaleidEO
text: KaleidEO is a subsidiary of SatSure, established in 2022 and headquartered in Bengaluru, India. The company focuses on developing high-resolution optical payloads for satellites, aiming to address challenges in imagery acquisition for various applications. KaleidEO has made significant strides in deploying edge computing technology in space, enabling real-time analysis of satellite imagery directly from orbiting satellites. This capability enhances the efficiency of data processing and allows for actionable insights to be generated quickly, which is crucial for applications such as national security and disaster response. The company plans to launch four satellites equipped with edge-computing capabilities by 2025, contributing to India's growing space technology ecosystem. KaleidEO's innovative approach includes the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms for tasks like cloud detection and change detection in satellite images.

title: Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI)
text: The Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) is South Korea's primary aeronautics and space agency, established in 1989. Located in Daejeon, KARI focuses on advancing the country's aerospace capabilities, including the development of launch vehicles, satellites, and unmanned aerial systems. The institute has been pivotal in several significant projects, such as the KSLV-2 launcher and the Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter (KPLO), which marks South Korea's first lunar exploration mission. KARI's vision includes enhancing indigenous launch capabilities, exploring the Moon, and developing environmentally friendly aircraft technologies. The institute also plays a crucial role in fostering collaboration between government, academia, and industry to strengthen the national space ecosystem. As of early 2024, KARI continues to lead advancements in satellite technology and space exploration initiatives, contributing to South Korea's emergence as a key player in the global space sector.

title: L3Harris Geospatial
text: L3Harris Geospatial Solutions, Inc. is a prominent provider of geospatial data and technology, specializing in image analysis, data visualization, and remote sensing solutions. Based in Broomfield, Colorado, the company has been delivering advanced geospatial products since 1951, catering to various industries including defense, agriculture, transportation, and environmental management.

title: Mapsense Technologies (OPC) Private Limited
text: Mapsense Technologies (OPC) Private Limited is an Indian startup founded on May 23, 2019, and headquartered in Gurgaon, Haryana. The company specializes in developing enterprise-grade products using geospatial technologies, focusing on location intelligence and real-time location tracking solutions for businesses of various sizes.

title: Marvel Geospatial Solutions Pvt Ltd.
text: Marvel Geospatial Solutions Pvt Ltd, established in 2008 and based in Hyderabad, India, specializes in providing comprehensive geospatial solutions, including data mapping and management services. The company integrates various technologies such as satellite and aerial remote sensing, GIS databases, and photogrammetry to support sectors like utilities, land administration, and transportation. With a workforce of around 100 employees, Marvel has earned recognition as a winner of the India 5000 Best MSME Awards in 2020. It is ISO 9001:2015 certified and serves a diverse clientele across Australia, Africa, the US, and the UAE. The company aims to enhance its global presence through innovative solutions and has recently ventured into drone manufacturing to expand its service offerings.

title: Maxar Technologies Inc.
text: Maxar Technologies Inc. is an American space technology company headquartered in Westminster, Colorado, specializing in advanced satellite imaging and geospatial services. Formed in 2017 through the merger of DigitalGlobe and MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates (MDA), Maxar operates a fleet of high-resolution Earth observation satellites, including the WorldView series, which provides critical data for applications in defense, telecommunications, climate research, and disaster response. The company offers a range of products and services, including Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging, Precision3D data suites, and on-demand intelligence solutions

title: MGGP Aero
text: MGGP Aero is a Polish company specializing in remote sensing data acquisition from airborne and satellite platforms. Established over 20 years ago, it focuses on providing high-resolution aerial imagery, LiDAR data, hyperspectral imaging, and thermal images. The company is actively involved in various sectors, including environmental monitoring and urban analysis, and has completed numerous projects across Europe, including Romania and Germany. MGGP Aero operates a diverse fleet of aircraft equipped with advanced sensors, enabling comprehensive geospatial solutions for clients. It is also engaged in research and development, collaborating with scientific institutions to innovate within the geoinformation industry. The company's headquarters are located in Tarnów, Poland.

title: Opegieka
text: OPEGIEKA Sp. z o.o. is a Polish company founded in 1989, specializing in geoinformatics and related services such as photogrammetry, remote sensing, geodesy, and cartography. Based in Elbląg, Poland, OPEGIEKA has established itself as a leader in the GEO/ICT market, providing innovative spatial information solutions for businesses, government agencies, and various sectors. The company holds several certifications, including ISO 9001 and ISO 27000, and operates its own data center. OPEGIEKA is involved in significant projects like the development of nationwide teleinformatics systems and has extensive experience in creating digital terrain models and topographic maps. It utilizes advanced technologies, including LiDAR and aerial surveying, to deliver high-quality geospatial data and services tailored to client needs.

title: OpalAi
text: OpalAi is a technology company specializing in spatial artificial intelligence, headquartered in Los Angeles, California. Founded with expertise drawn from NASA, OpalAi focuses on transforming complex satellite and SAR imagery into actionable insights for various applications, such as vehicle detection and wildfire monitoring. Their core offerings include innovative solutions like ScanToBIM, which generates detailed Building Information Models from point cloud data, and ScanTo3D, enabling real-time creation of 2D and 3D CAD models. The company aims to enhance decision-making processes across industries such as real estate, insurance, and transportation by leveraging advanced AI technologies. OpalAi emphasizes collaboration between AI systems and professionals to tackle intricate challenges in dynamic environments.

title: Piersight
text: Piersight is a space technology company founded in 2023 and based in Ahmedabad, India, specializing in surveillance solutions for the maritime industry. The company focuses on developing a constellation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Automatic Identification System (AIS) satellites to provide persistent monitoring of ocean activities. Piersight's services cater to various sectors, including shipping, maritime insurance, defense, and environmental protection, offering all-weather imaging and low-latency actionable insights. The company has raised a total of $6.72 million in funding, with its latest round being a seed investment. Key founders Gaurav Seth and Vinit Bansal bring extensive experience from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the defense sector. Piersight is also part of the Techstars Space Accelerator program, collaborating with prominent organizations like NASA and the United States Space Force to enhance its technological capabilities.

title: Pixxel
text: Pixxel is an Indian space technology startup based in Bengaluru, focused on developing a constellation of hyperspectral imaging satellites. Founded in 2018 and backed by Google, Pixxel aims to provide high-resolution Earth observation data with applications across various sectors, including agriculture, environmental monitoring, mining, and defense. The company recently achieved a significant milestone by successfully launching three of its six satellites as part of the Firefly constellation aboard a SpaceX rocket on January 15, 2025. These satellites are designed to capture detailed imagery across hundreds of light bands, enabling precise monitoring of natural resources and environmental changes. Pixxel plans to expand its constellation with an additional 18 satellites.

title: Planet Labs
text: Planet Labs PBC, founded in 2010 by former NASA scientists, is an American Earth imaging company based in San Francisco. It operates a fleet of small satellites called Doves, which capture daily high-resolution images of the Earth for various applications, including agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. The company went public in 2021 through a merger with DMY Technology Group IV, valuing it at approximately $2.8 billion. As a Public Benefit Corporation, Planet Labs is dedicated to making global changes visible and actionable through its satellite data services.

title: Rolta India
text: Rolta India Limited is an Indian multinational technology company headquartered in Mumbai, specializing in innovative IT solutions across various sectors, including government, utilities, oil and gas, and healthcare. Founded in 1982, Rolta has developed a strong portfolio of products and services based on its proprietary intellectual property (IP), focusing on areas such as business intelligence (BI), big data analytics, geospatial visualization, and cloud solutions.

title: ROSCOSMOS
text: ROSCOSMOS, officially known as the State Corporation for Space Activities "Roscosmos," is the governmental body responsible for managing Russia's space program, established in 2015 through the merger of the Federal Space Agency and the United Rocket and Space Corporation. Headquartered in Moscow, ROSCOSMOS oversees a wide range of activities including human spaceflight, satellite operations, and space exploration, playing a significant role in the International Space Station (ISS) program and developing missions to explore celestial bodies like the Moon and Mars. The organization operates several launch facilities, notably the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan and the Vostochny Cosmodrome in Russia's Far East.

title: Satellogic
text: Satellogic Inc., founded in 2010 by Emiliano Kargieman and Gerardo Richarte, is a leading Earth observation company focused on providing high-resolution satellite imagery and geospatial data. Headquartered in New York and with R&D facilities in Argentina, Satellogic has developed a scalable constellation of satellites designed to remap the entire planet frequently and affordably. As of early 2024, the company operates 26 satellites and aims to expand its fleet to over 200. The company's mission is to democratize access to geospatial data to address global challenges like climate change and food security, making it a key player in the remote sensing industry.

title: Satpalda Geospatial Services
text: Satpalda Geospatial Services is a prominent provider of satellite imagery and geospatial solutions, established in 2019 and based in Delhi, India. The company specializes in delivering high-resolution satellite imagery and a wide range of geospatial services, including photogrammetry, digital surface models (DSM), and digital terrain models (DTM).

title: SatSure
text: SatSure is a Bengaluru-based deep-tech startup founded in 2017, specializing in decision intelligence through the integration of satellite remote sensing, machine learning, and big data analytics. The company focuses on providing actionable insights across various sectors, including agriculture, infrastructure, and climate action. By leveraging satellite imagery combined with additional data sources, SatSure aims to enhance decision-making processes related to agricultural finance, infrastructure monitoring, and climate change mitigation. The company is recognized for its innovative approach to commercializing space data and has established itself as a key player in the Indian space technology ecosystem.

title: SATIM Inc
text: SATIM Inc., founded in 2012 and headquartered in Burlingame, California, is a technology company specializing in object detection and classification using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite imagery. The company operates primarily in the defense, security, and commercial sectors, providing services that accurately detect and classify various objects such as military vessels and aircraft. SATIM has developed advanced AI-based software solutions and simulators for generating synthetic SAR signatures, enhancing the capabilities of SAR data analysis. In recent developments, SATIM signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Digilogic Systems to co-develop a Synthetic Aperture Radar Environment Simulator, aimed at improving testing processes for SAR payloads. The company has partnered with the European Space Agency and is recognized for its innovation in automatic object detection technologies.

title: Skywatch
text: SkyWatch is a Canadian company founded in 2014, based in Kitchener, Ontario, that specializes in Earth observation (EO) data aggregation and management. The company provides a platform called EarthCache, which allows users to easily access and integrate satellite imagery and geospatial data into their applications and workflows. SkyWatch aims to democratize remote sensing data by offering a modern API for high-volume data access, thereby facilitating its use across various sectors such as agriculture, environmental monitoring, and critical infrastructure. Additionally, SkyWatch operates TerraStream, an automated data distribution platform for satellite operators, enabling them to deliver their data products directly to customers.

title: Space Applications Centre (SAC)
text: The Space Applications Centre (SAC) is a key research and development institution under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), located in Ahmedabad, India. Established in 1972, SAC focuses on the development and application of space technology across various fields, including telecommunications, remote sensing, meteorology, and satellite navigation. The center is responsible for creating payloads for communication satellites like the Indian National Satellite (INSAT) and the Geo-Stationary Satellite (GSAT) series, which support services such as broadcasting, internet, and telecommunication. SAC also plays a significant role in scientific missions, contributing to projects like Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission. With advanced facilities for payload integration, environmental testing, and data processing, SAC collaborates with national and international institutions to enhance its research capabilities. Additionally, it offers training programs for students from the Asia-Pacific region in satellite meteorology and communication under the Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in Asia and the Pacific (CSSTEAP).

title: Space Imaging Middle East
text: Space Imaging Middle East (SIME) is a leading provider of satellite and aerial imagery services in the Middle East, established in 1997 and headquartered in the United Arab Emirates. As a regional affiliate of DigitalGlobe, SIME plays a significant role in the geospatial and GIS solutions market across the Middle East, Persian Gulf, Eastern Africa, and Central Asia. IME utilizes a wide range of satellite constellations and aerial sensors to deliver its products. The company has established partnerships with leading technology firms to enhance its service offerings. Its ground station in the UAE controls the satellite operations, ensuring efficient data collection and processing.

title: Spire Global Inc.
text: Spire Global Inc. is a satellite-powered data company headquartered in Vienna, Virginia, specializing in providing high-frequency weather data, ship tracking, and other analytics services. Founded in 2012, Spire operates a large constellation of nanosatellites, known as LEMUR (Low Earth Multi-Use Receiver), which allows for comprehensive monitoring of maritime and aviation activities, as well as weather patterns. The company's data is utilized across various sectors, including maritime domain awareness, trade monitoring, and search and rescue operations. Spire's innovative approach combines machine learning and predictive analytics to deliver actionable insights to clients such as government authorities, marine companies, and port operators.

title: Trimble
text: Trimble Inc. is a global technology company founded in 1978, headquartered in Westminster, Colorado. It specializes in providing software, hardware, and services that enhance productivity across various industries, including construction, agriculture, geospatial, and transportation. Trimble's core technologies encompass positioning, modeling, connectivity, and data analytics, which connect the physical and digital worlds to improve efficiency and sustainability. The company is known for its innovations in global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), machine control, and cloud-based solutions. Trimble operates over 150 locations worldwide and has made significant acquisitions to expand its capabilities, including the purchase of SketchUp from Google in 2012. As of 2024, Trimble continues to lead in transforming critical industries through advanced technology solutions.

title: Topcon Positioning Systems
text: Topcon Positioning Systems, a subsidiary of Topcon Corporation, is a leading provider of precision measurement and workflow solutions for the construction, geospatial, and agriculture sectors. Established in 1994 and headquartered in Livermore, California, Topcon specializes in technologies such as GNSS receivers, total stations, machine control systems, and 3D scanning solutions. The company aims to enhance productivity and efficiency through innovative technologies that integrate high-precision measurement with software and data. Topcon's mission focuses on delivering end-to-end solutions that meet the global demand for sustainable infrastructure and agriculture. The company has a strong presence worldwide, with operations in various countries and a commitment to research and development to advance its product offerings.

title: Umbra
text: Umbra is a U.S.-based commercial space technology company founded in 2015, specializing in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite systems. Headquartered in Santa Barbara, California, Umbra operates a constellation designed to provide high-resolution imagery for various applications, including intelligence, defense, and disaster response. The first satellite, Umbra-01, was launched in June 2021, and the company plans to expand its fleet to 32 satellites. Umbra's SAR technology allows for all-weather and day-and-night monitoring capabilities, making it a valuable resource for both commercial and governmental clients. Recently, Umbra has been awarded contracts by the Space Development Agency to integrate its remote sensing capabilities into future space architectures, further solidifying its role in the evolving landscape of satellite imagery and geospatial intelligence.

title: Walphot Sa
text: Walphot proposes products and services in the area of geomatics since more than 30 years. Walphot is qualified for the whole production line of geographic data from the capture of the information (spaceborne or airborne) to the delivery of specific products (maps, reports,…) or integrated services (Geographic Information Systems). Walphot already participated in the 80ís to the first large project using satellite data (CORINE-program).

title: Satpalda Geospatial Services
text: Satpalda Geospatial Services is a prominent provider of satellite imagery and geospatial solutions, established in 2019 and based in Delhi, India. The company specializes in delivering high-resolution satellite imagery and a wide range of geospatial services, including photogrammetry, digital surface models (DSM), and digital terrain models (DTM).

title: European Space Agency
text: The European Space Agency (ESA) is an intergovernmental organization established in 1975, dedicated to space exploration and technology development. Headquartered in Paris, ESA comprises 23 member states and coordinates their financial and intellectual resources to undertake projects that exceed the capabilities of individual nations. Its mission encompasses a wide range of activities, including Earth observation, navigation, telecommunications, and human and robotic exploration of space. ESA is known for its significant contributions to international space missions, such as participation in the International Space Station (ISS) program and various planetary exploration initiatives. The agency operates several key facilities, including the European Space Research and Technology Centre (ESTEC) in the Netherlands and the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Germany. With an annual budget of approximately €11 billion as of 2023, ESA continues to play a crucial role in advancing Europe’s capabilities in space science and technology while collaborating with global partners.

title: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
text: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is an independent agency of the United States federal government, established on July 29, 1958, to oversee the nation's civilian space program and aeronautics research. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., NASA is responsible for a wide range of activities, including human and robotic space exploration, satellite development, and scientific research related to Earth and the universe. The agency has been instrumental in numerous landmark missions, such as the Apollo Moon landings, the Space Shuttle program, and the ongoing International Space Station (ISS) operations. NASA's organizational structure comprises four main directorates: Aeronautics Research, Science, Space Technology, and Human Exploration and Operations. With a rich history of innovation and exploration, NASA continues to lead efforts in advancing space technology and understanding the cosmos through missions like the Mars rovers and the James Webb Space Telescope

title: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)
text: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is a scientific agency of the United States government, established on October 3, 1970, under the Department of Commerce. NOAA is responsible for understanding and predicting changes in climate, weather, oceans, and coasts, which includes forecasting weather, monitoring oceanic and atmospheric conditions, and conducting research to protect marine resources and manage fisheries. The agency comprises six major offices: the National Weather Service (NWS), which provides weather forecasts and warnings; the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), focused on managing coastal fisheries; the National Ocean Service (NOS), which addresses ocean health; the National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), responsible for environmental data dissemination; the Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (OAR), conducting environmental research; and the Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO). NOAA operates numerous research laboratories across the country and plays a crucial role in severe weather preparedness and environmental stewardship.

title: Synspective
text: Synspective is a Japanese company founded in 2018 that develops and operates a constellation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites, aiming to build a fleet of 30 SAR satellites by the late 2020s. The company combines its own SAR data with analytics solutions to enable near real-time monitoring of Earth for applications such as disaster response, infrastructure monitoring, and urban development, positioning itself as a key player in Japan's growing SAR ecosystem.

title: Satellite Vu
text: Satellite Vu is a United Kingdom-based space technology company specializing in high-resolution thermal infrared imaging from small satellites, complemented by optical Earth observation services. The company's thermal data supports applications including energy efficiency monitoring, industrial asset tracking, wildfire detection, and climate-related analytics, aiming to deliver near real-time global thermal imagery.

title: Airbus Defence and Space
text: Airbus Defence and Space, a division of the Airbus Group with major operations in France and Germany, is a leading operator of Earth observation satellites, including the TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X synthetic aperture radar missions developed with the German Aerospace Center (DLR). The division provides high-resolution SAR and optical imagery, geospatial data, and analytics for defense, security, and commercial applications worldwide.

title: MDA Space
text: MDA Space (formerly MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates) is a Canadian robotics, satellite systems, and geointelligence company with over 55 years of history and more than 450 missions. MDA operates the RADARSAT and RADARSAT Constellation Mission SAR satellite programs for the Canadian government, providing radar data and geospatial solutions for maritime surveillance, disaster management, and environmental monitoring.

title: e-GEOS
text: e-GEOS, a joint venture between the Italian Space Agency (ASI) and Telespazio (Leonardo/Thales), is headquartered in Italy and specializes in the distribution and analysis of data from the COSMO-SkyMed constellation of SAR satellites. The company delivers Earth observation products and geospatial services for defense, intelligence, and commercial markets from its centers in Matera, Italy and Neustrelitz, Germany.

title: Orbital Insight
text: Orbital Insight, founded in 2013 and based in Palo Alto, California, is a geospatial analytics and location intelligence company that uses AI to derive insights from multiple sources of Earth observation data, including satellite imagery. Its analytics support use cases such as supply chain monitoring, global commodities tracking, geopolitical risk assessment, and national security.

title: UP42
text: UP42, headquartered in Berlin, Germany, operates a marketplace and developer platform that makes it easier to find, buy, and use geospatial data, including SAR and optical satellite imagery, from a wide range of providers. The platform enables organizations of all sizes to access and combine Earth observation datasets and analytics through a single, unified API.

title: Geospatial Intelligence Pty Ltd
text: Geospatial Intelligence Pty Ltd, founded in 2002 and headquartered in Canberra, Australia, is a 100% Australian-owned company specializing in the sourcing and analysis of very high-resolution optical, multispectral, and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite imagery. The company delivers value-added geospatial products combining imagery with AIS and open-source intelligence for defense, environmental, and commercial clients, and is an official distributor of Synspective's SAR data products in Australia.

title: Ananth Technologies
text: Ananth Technologies, founded in 1992 and based in Hyderabad, India, is a pioneer in space and defence manufacturing, producing critical aerospace systems and components that have supported around 50 launch vehicles in partnership with ISRO and global aerospace leaders. The company also provides high-value geospatial services, with its facilities certified under AS 9100C and ISO 9001:2008.

title: Kawa Space
text: Kawa Space is an Indian space-tech company building foundational Earth observation infrastructure, including satellite-based datasets, a processing stack, and an application layer for geospatial analytics. The company's platform is engineered for real-time spectrum intelligence, imagery fusion, automated geolocation, and strategic domain awareness, serving global intelligence and national security customers.

title: GalaxEye
text: GalaxEye is an Indian space-tech startup developing the world's first multi-sensor imaging satellite under its Drishti Mission, aiming to fuse Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and optical imagery on a single platform. This fusion approach is designed to overcome the limitations of cloud cover and darkness that affect purely optical Earth observation systems, delivering more reliable, all-weather imagery.

title: German Aerospace Center (DLR)
text: The German Aerospace Center (Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt, DLR) is Germany's national aeronautics and space research centre, employing around 12,000 people from over 100 nations. DLR developed and operates the TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X synthetic aperture radar satellite missions in partnership with Airbus Defence and Space, generating high-precision global elevation models and radar imagery used in research, environmental monitoring, and security applications.

title: Canadian Space Agency
text: The Canadian Space Agency (CSA) is Canada's national space agency, responsible for the country's space program including the RADARSAT and RADARSAT Constellation Mission synthetic aperture radar satellites, operated in partnership with MDA Space. These SAR missions support maritime surveillance, disaster response, and Arctic and environmental monitoring for Canada and its international partners.

title: Introduction to Remote Sensing
text: Arthur P. Cracknell | Physical principles, satellite systems, lidar, SAR applications. A comprehensive guide to satellite remote sensing techniques, image interpretation, and current applications in Earth observation.

title: Remote Sensing: Principles and Applications
text: B C Panda | Core principles, sensor technologies, data interpretation. Detailed exploration of electromagnetic theory, sensor design, and practical case studies across varied environments.

title: Introduction to Geospatial Technologies
text: Bradley A. Shellito, January 1, 2011 by W H Freeman & Co | Combining both theoretical coverage and hands-on lab work, and accessible to majors and non-majors alike, Bradley Shellito's Introduction to Geospatial Technologies has become a new favorite for the digital Earth course. The new edition reflects the latest developments in the field, including how scientists are using GIS data with cloud technology. With lab activities that utilize both widely available freeware and ArcGIS, instructors can tailor the course to their students. Introduction to Geospatial Technologies, Second Edition is available in three a paperback edition, a loose-leaf edition, and a fully interactive e-Book.

title: Remote Sensing and GIS
text: Basudeb Bhatta March 27, 2008 by Oxford University Press | The book provides an exhaustive coverage of optical, thermal, and microwave remote sensing, global navigation satellite systems (e.g., GPS), digital photogrammetry, and visual image analysis. The main emphasis is on the basic concepts of remote sensing and GIS but topics such as digital imageprocessing, spatial and attribute data model, geospatial analysis, and planning, implementation, and management of GIS have also been discussed in detail. Owing to its lucid style and presentation of advanced topics, such as ground truth data, metadata concepts, latest developments and modern trends of GIS and GNSS, makes this book suitable as a reference for postgraduate students and practicing professionals from the Geomatics community.

title: Physical Fundamentals of Remote Sensing
text: E. Schanda Springer-Verlag | Ten years ago the author, together with eight co-authors, edited a textbook Remote Sensing for Environmental Sciences within the series on Ecological Studies of Springer-Verlag. At that time there were not yet many books available on remote sensing. The decade that has elapsed was marked by a spectacular development in this field. This development took place in many by widening the areas of application, by improvements of the methods and the sensors, by the introduction of new versatile platforms, but also by deepening the knowledge of the theoretical foundations. This evolution improved the ability to explain the interaction between electromagnetic radia­ tion and natural objects, which, in its turn, allowed for better modelization and for the creation of refined mathematical tools in the processing of remotely sensed data and in the determination of the physical status of remote objects. The community of research workers engaged in development and use of remote sensing methods changed accordingly from a modest group of scientists in the early 1970's to a considerable branch of specialized and interdisciplinary activity. The training of students had to be adapted to cope with the increasing number of people entering this new field and with the increasing quality of the material to be presented

title: Hyperspectral Remote Sensing: Principles and Applications
text: Marcus Borengasser, William S. Hungate, Russell Watkins, Published: 16 February 2023 | Description: Land management issues, such as mapping tree species, recognizing invasive plants, and identifying key geologic features, require an understanding of complex technical issues before the best decisions can be made. Hyperspectral remote sensing is one the technologies that can help with reliable detection and identification. Presenting the fundamentals of remote sensing at an introductory level, Hyperspectral Remote Sensing: Principles and Applications explores all major aspects of hyperspectral image acquisition, exploitation, interpretation, and applications.The book begins with several chapters on the basic concepts and underlying principles of remote sensing images. It introduces spectral radiometry concepts, such as radiance, irradiance, flux, and blackbody radiation; covers imaging spectrometers, examining spectral range, full width half maximum (FWHM), resolution, sampling, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and multispectral and hyperspectral sensor systems; and addresses atmospheric interactions. The book then discusses information extraction, with chapters covering the underlying physics principles that lead to the creation of an image and the interpretation of the image's information. The final chapters describe case studies that illustrate the use of hyperspectral remote sensing in agriculture, environmental monitoring, forestry, and geology. After reading this book, you will have a better understanding of how to evaluate different approaches to hyperspectral analyses and to determine which approaches will work for your applications.

title: Remote Sensing of Global Croplands for Food Security
text: Prasad Thenkabail, John G. Lyon, Hugh Turral, Chandrashekhar Biradar | Increases in populations have created an increasing demand for food crops while increases in demand for biofuels have created an increase in demand for fuel crops. What has not increased is the amount of croplands and their productivity. These and many other factors such as decreasing water resources in a changing climate have created a crisis like situation in global food security. Decision makers in these situations need accurate information based on science. Remote Sensing of Global Croplands for Food Security provides a comprehensive knowledge base in use of satellite sensor-based maps and statistics that can be used to develop strategies for croplands (irrigated and rainfed) and their water use for food security.Over 50 Multi-disciplinary Global Experts Give Insight and Provide Practical ApproachesEmphasizing practical mapping technologies based on advanced remote sensing data and methods, this book provides approaches for estimating irrigated and rainfed cropland areas and their water use on a national, continental, or global basis. Written by 50+ leading experts working at the forefront of this critical area, it offers case studies from a variety of continents highlighting the subtle requirements of each. In a very practical way it demonstrates the experience, utility, and models for determining water resources used and resulting yields of irrigated and rainfed croplands. The authors discuss: (a) innovative methods used for mapping croplands, (b) approaches adopted to collect cropland data in different countries by traditional and non-traditional means, (c) accuracies, uncertainties, and errors involved in producing cropland products, (d) surface energy balance models used to assess crop water use, and (e) extensive results and outcomes pertaining to global croplands and their water use.Develop Strategies for an Enhanced Green Revolution and an Accelerated Blue RevolutionLinking croplands to water use and food security, the book provides a global perspective on this sensitive issue. It gives insight into the extent of cropland usage, their spatial distribution, their cropping intensities, and their water use patterns. The editors collect the experience, methods, models, and results that show the way forward and help in decision-making on water resources and food security. All of this is required for developing strategies for an enhanced green revolution and for an accelerated blue revolution.

title: Satellite Remote Sensing for Conservation Action: Case Studies from Aquatic and Terrestrial Ecosystems
text: Graeme M. Buchanan (editor) September 27, 2018 by Cambridge University Press | Satellite remote sensing presents an amazing opportunity to inform biodiversity conservation by inexpensively gathering repeated monitoring information for vast areas of the Earth. However, these observations first need processing and interpretation if they are to inform conservation action. Through a series of case studies, this book presents detailed examples of the application of satellite remote sensing, covering both aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, to conservation. The authors describe how collaboration between the remote sensing and conservation communities makes satellite data functional for operational conservation and provide concrete examples of the lessons learned in addition to the scientific details. The editors, one at NASA and the other at a conservation NGO, have brought together leading researchers in conservation remote sensing to share their experiences from project development through to application, and emphasise the human side of these projects.

title: Remote Sensing of Protected Lands
text: Yeqiao Wang, Published: 18 October 2019 | National parks, wildlife refuges and sanctuaries, natural reserves, conservation areas, frontier lands, and marine-protected areas are increasingly recognized as essential providers of ecosystem services and biological resources. As debates about climate change and sustainability intensify, protected areas become more important as indicators of ecosystem conditions in particular environments or in comparison with adjacent environments.The first book of its kind, Remote Sensing of Protected Lands showcases state-of-the-art remote sensing applications for the inventory and monitoring of protected areas. Contributions from renowned scholars and experts from around the world are organized into four sections covering the use of remote sensing in:Changing landscapes and change detectionInventory, mapping, and conservation Inventory and monitoring of frontier lands Decision support for the management of protected lands

title: Remote Sensing and GIS for Ecologists: Using Open Source Software
text: Martin Wegmann(Editor),Benjamin Leutner(Editor),Stefan Dech(Editor) March 21, 2016 by Pelagic Publishing | This is a book about how ecologists can integrate remote sensing and GIS in their daily work. It will allow ecologists to get started with the application of remote sensing and to understand its potential and limitations. Using practical examples, the book covers all necessary steps from planning field campaigns to deriving ecologically relevant information through remote sensing and modelling of species distributions. All practical examples in this book rely on OpenSource software and freely available data sets. Quantum GIS (QGIS) is introduced for basic GIS data handling, and in-depth spatial analytics and statistics are conducted with the software packages R and GRASS. Readers will learn how to apply remote sensing within ecological research projects, how to approach spatial data sampling and how to interpret remote sensing derived products. The authors discuss a wide range of statistical analyses with regard to satellite data as well as specialised topics such as time-series analysis. Extended scripts on how to create professional looking maps and graphics are also provided. This book is a valuable resource for students and scientists in the fields of conservation and ecology interested in learning how to get started in applying remote sensing in ecological research and conservation planning.

title: Introduction to the Physics And Techniques of Remote Sensing
text: Charles Elachi, Jakob J. Van Zyl,January 1, 2006 by Wiley-Interscience | The Second Edition of this authoritative book offers readers the essential science and engineering foundation needed to understand remote sensing and apply it in real-world situations. Thoroughly updated to reflect the tremendous technological leaps made since the publication of the first edition, this book covers the gamut of knowledge and skills needed to work in this dynamic field, including: Physics involved in wave-matter interaction, the building blocks for interpreting data Techniques used to collect data Remote sensing applications The authors have carefully structured and organized the book to introduce readers to the basics, and then move on to more advanced applications. Following an introduction, Chapter 2 sets forth the basic properties of electromagnetic waves and their interactions with matter. Chapters 3 through 7 cover the use of remote sensing in solid surface studies, including oceans. Each chapter covers one major part of the electromagnetic spectrum (e.g., visible/near infrared, thermal infrared, passive microwave, and active microwave).Chapters 8 through 12 then cover remote sensing in the study of atmospheres and ionospheres. Each chapter first presents the basic interaction mechanism, followed by techniques to acquire, measure, and study the information, or waves, emanating from the medium under investigation. In most cases, a specific advanced sensor is used for illustration.The book is generously illustrated with fifty percent new figures. Numerous illustrations are reproduced in a separate section of color plates. Examples of data acquired from spaceborne sensors are included throughout. Finally, a set of exercises is provided.This book is based on an upper-level undergraduate and first-year graduate course taught by the authors at the California Institute of Technology. Because of the multidisciplinary nature of the field and its applications, it is appropriate for students in electrical engineering, applied physics, geology, planetary science, astronomy, and aeronautics. It is also recommended for any engineer or scientist interested in working in this exciting field.

title: Applied Spatial Data Analysis with R
text: Roger S.; Pebesma Bivand, January 1, 2008 by Springer | This book addresses the needs of researchers and students using R to analyze spatial data across a range of disciplines and professions. The book is co-authored by a group involved in the Comprehensive R Archive Network.

title: Photogrammetry, GIS & Remote Sensing
text: S S Manugula,Veeranna Bommakanti, February 4, 2018 by Ebooks2go Inc | This book has been written for use in classrooms by both the instructor and the students and also for independent study in the coming decades. The main intention for writing this book is to make the subject very easy at the same time the to cover the syllabus for undergraduate. The basic concepts of Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing & GIS all are included in a single book which helps the students to the face the exams quickly and very easily. This book is intended to be basically utilized as a quick reference in support to various text books.

title: Multi-purposeful Application of Geospatial Data
text: Rustam B. Rustamov, Sabina Hasanova, Mahfuza H. Zeynalova, Published: 09 May 2018 | This book is dedicated toward space technology application in Earth studies based on the use of a variety of methods for satellite information classification and interpretation. Advantages of geospatial data use in a large-scale area of observation and monitoring as a source of decision-making stage have been demonstrated. The book describes navigation systems providing data estimation method and review of existing data in the literature relevant to remote sensing sensors delivering main information electromagnetic spectrum and a variety of sensor applications. This aspect is important when combining/integrating satellite data processing into the field measurements. Satellites and satellite data application for the study of Earth features have been demonstrated as the next step of geospatial data application. The use of different purposeful processing technology applications of satellite data is one of the vital aspects of space technology advances. The use of GNSS GPS technology in industry and MODIS images and data interpretation for agriculture purposes has been presented. It was the aim of the book to create an attractive environment by presenting space technology application in the wide areas of Earth study. For this purpose, some of the book chapters are dedicated toward space technology advances in climate monitoring, natural disaster factor detection, satellite data processing optimization, and GIS technology for meteorology information with the aim of agriculture developments.

title: Infrared Technology Fundamentals
text: Monroe Schlessinger,September 13, 1994 by Routledge | This work provides a basic understanding of the physical background and engineering considerations required for the design of IR systems, examining all components and combining them into examples of current surveillance systems. This second edition presents: new coverage of state-of-the-art optical systems, including lightweight mirrors and adaptive optics; planar-hybrid and Z-technology focal planes; the design of a ground-based IR astronomical telescope and the performance equations of laser-radar systems; and more.

title: Introductory Digital Image Processing
text: John R. Jensen May 10, 2004 by Prentice Hall | For junior/graduate-level courses in Remote Sensing in Geography, Geology, Forestry, and Biology. This revision of Introductory Digital Image Processing: A Remote Sensing Perspective continues to focus on digital image processing of aircraft- and satellite-derived, remotely sensed data for Earth resource management applications. Extensively illustrated, it explains how to extract biophysical information from remote sensor data for almost all multidisciplinary land-based environmental projects. Part of the Prentice Hall Series Geographic Information Science.

title: Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis: An Introduction
text: John A. Richards December 2, 2005 by Springer |  Revised and enlarged to reflect new developments in the field, the fourth edition of this well-established text provides an introduction to quantitative evaluation of satellite- and aircraft-derived remotely retrieved data. Each chapter covers the pros and cons of digital remotely sensed data, without detailed mathematical treatment of computer based algorithms, but in a manner conductive to an understanding of their capabilities and limitations.

title: Multispectral Image Analysis Using the Object-Oriented Paradigm
text: P. S. Thenkabail, J. G. Lyon, H. Turral, C. Biradar | Bringing a fresh new perspective to remote sensing, object-based image analysis is a paradigm shift from the traditional pixel-based approach. Featuring various practical examples to provide understanding of this new modus operandi, Multispectral Image Analysis Using the Object-Oriented Paradigm reviews the current image analysis methods and demonstrates advantages to improve information extraction from imagery. This reference describes traditional image analysis techniques, introduces object-oriented technology, and discusses the benefits of object-based versus pixel-based classification. It examines the creation of object primitives using image segmentation approaches and the use of various techniques for object classification. The author covers image enhancement methods, how to use ancillary data to constrain image segmentation, and concepts of semantic grouping of objects. He concludes by addressing accuracy assessment approaches. The accompanying downloadable resources present sample data that enable the use of different approaches to problem solving. Integrating remote sensing techniques and GIS analysis, Multispectral Image Analysis Using the Object-Oriented Paradigm distills new tools to extract information from remotely sensed data

title: Hyperspectral Remote Sensing: Fundamentals and Practices
text: Ruiliang Pu,Published: 15 December 201 | Advanced imaging spectral technology and hyperspectral analysis techniques for multiple applications are the key features of the book. This book will present in one volume complete solutions from concepts, fundamentals, and methods of acquisition of hyperspectral data to analyses and applications of the data in a very coherent manner. It will help readers to fully understand basic theories of HRS, how to utilize various field spectrometers and bioinstruments, the importance of radiometric correction and atmospheric correction, the use of analysis, tools and software, and determine what to do with HRS technology and data.

title: Introduction to Microwave Remote Sensing
text: Iain H. Woodhouse |  Introduction to Microwave Remote Sensing offers an extensive overview of this versatile and extremely precise technology for technically oriented undergraduates and graduate students. This textbook emphasizes an important shift in conceptualization and directs it toward students with prior knowledge of optical remote the author dispels any linkage between microwave and optical remote sensing. Instead, he constructs the concept of microwave remote sensing by comparing it to the process of audio perception, explaining the workings of the ear as a metaphor for microwave instrumentation. This volume takes an “application-driven” approach. Instead of describing the technology and then its uses, this textbook justifies the need for measurement then explains how microwave technology addresses this need. Following a brief summary of the field and a history of the use of microwaves, the book explores the physical properties of microwaves and the polarimetric properties of electromagnetic waves. It examines the interaction of microwaves with matter, analyzes passive atmospheric and passive surface measurements, and describes the operation of altimeters and scatterometers. The textbook concludes by explaining how high resolution images are created using radars, and how techniques of interferometry can be applied to both passive and active sensors.

title: Remote Sensing of Coastal Environments
